newsitem.title: USA: Lira level satisfactory for economy - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Lira level satisfactory for economy - Dini.

text.p: DENVER, JUNE 22 (REUTER) - The lira's current levels are satisfactory, Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Sunday. Dini also reaffirmed Rome's firm intention to join the European single currency from the planned start in 1999.

"I don't want to second-guess markets, but we consider an exchange rate close to the present one to be satisfactory for our economy", Dini told reporters at a summit of the Group of Seven industrialized countries and Russia. The lira is currently quoted at 979 to the mark and 1,689 to the dollar.
"The fundamentals of our economy are strong, though certainly a bit weak on the side of growth and domestic demand, but this is dictated by the other objectives Italy is pursuing," Dini added.
"Italy is trying to stay within the Maastricht criteria because Italy wants to be in the monetary union from the start", he said.
Dini also defined as "generally satisfactory" the economic and financial situation of the industrial world.
"Moreover, this (growth) is taking place in a climate of financial stability, including exchange rates stability, which in the past was a trouble spot."

"Most industrial nations are on a path of stability-oriented policies, including a fight against inflation" Dini said, noting that inflation has never been lower in the past 30 years than it is today.
"This sets out a good basis for a better economic performance in all of our countries, especially in Europe," he added.
